notes: Each finding is one (file, algorithm family) pair. Line numbers are resolved from 'anchors' by tools/build_expected.py.
The first anchor is the primary usage site. Any anchor line (+/-1) counts as line-accurate.
'alt_files' lists other files where reporting the finding also counts (e.g. the config file that names the algorithm).
'also_ok' lists families that may be reported in a file without counting as false positives (e.g. the SHA-256 inside SHA256withRSA).
Any file under corpus/ with no findings is a negative control: every scanner finding there is a false positive.
Tier 4 findings without anchors are file-level (binary or PEM assets); line accuracy isn't judged for them.
'requires_password' marks findings only visible after opening a keystore; the password is the Java default.
'materials' describes the certificates and keys behind Tier 4 findings, so the reference CBOM can model them as certificate and related-crypto-material components.
Tier 5 compiled findings are attributed to the archive or bytecode file; a scanner may report 'x.jar!/path/Inner.class' and it still matches.
The 'pqc' category is scored as its own bucket. Hybrid TLS/SSH groups (X25519MLKEM768 etc.) are families in their own right; in code, an application-level hybrid is scored as its two components.
Tier 5 also ships a minified JavaScript bundle, a ProGuard-obfuscated jar and a stripped native binary; their sources are under tier5-sources/, outside the corpus.

decoys.corpus/tier1/python/t1_rsa.py: Comment mentions ML-DSA. Reporting a PQC algorithm here is a false positive (and a flattering one).
decoys.corpus/tier1/python/t1_modern_curves.py: Comment mentions X25519MLKEM768. Reporting ML-KEM here is a false positive.
decoys.corpus/negatives/python/n_strings_and_co: Algorithm names in docstrings, UI labels, log messages and identifiers; CRC32, base64 and hash() are not crypto.
decoys.corpus/negatives/python/n_test_vectors.p: Known-answer digest values stored as constants; a class named RSABadgeRenderer.
decoys.corpus/negatives/java/NStringsAndComment: Algorithm names in Javadoc, a label list and an error message; CRC32 and Base64 are not crypto.
decoys.corpus/negatives/java/NLookalikes.java: RsaBadgeRenderer, an enum of TLS cipher-suite names used only as labels, a SHA-256 constant, Adler32.
decoys.corpus/tier4/assets/tls/nginx.conf: Commented-out 'ssl_protocols SSLv3 TLSv1' and an RC4 cipher line. Reporting SSL-3.0 or RC4 is a false positive.
decoys.corpus/tier4/assets/ssh/sshd_config: A comment mentions removing ssh-rsa; the active HostKeyAlgorithms line is the finding.
decoys.corpus/negatives/assets/cert-rotation-ru: Runbook prose plus a truncated, redacted PEM block and example nginx lines inside Markdown.
decoys.corpus/negatives/assets/upload_validator: Valid PEM armor around base64 that is not DER. A scanner must not invent a certificate.
decoys.corpus/negatives/python/n_fibonacci_hash: Uses 0x9E3779B9, TEA's round constant, as a Fibonacci-hashing multiplier. Constant-matching scanners flag it.
decoys.corpus/negatives/python/n_iban_check.py: pow(base, exp, mod) for the IBAN mod-97 check: the same call textbook RSA uses.
decoys.corpus/negatives/java/NPrimeCapacity.jav: BigInteger.modPow in a Miller-Rabin test that sizes a hash table.
decoys.corpus/pqc/python/pq_washing.py: Docstring and identifiers claim ML-KEM-768; the code is ECDH on P-256. Any PQ finding here is an over-claim.
decoys.corpus/pqc/java/PqWashing.java: Class comment and field names claim ML-KEM-1024; the code is ECDH on P-384.
decoys.corpus/pqc/assets/tls/nginx_pq_washing.c: Comments claim hybrid ML-KEM key exchange; ssl_ecdh_curve lists only classical groups.
